subject: Next steps: procurement & commercial path for Redwood (hosted/dedicated/private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@acmeretail.com>, James O'Leary <james.oleary@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps (procurement & commercial path)

Hi Sofia / James —

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the team and hear more about Acme's pilot goals for personalized search and catalog summarization. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up procurement and pricing: 

1) Procurement readiness:
- Preferred payment method: you mentioned Procurement prefers PO / Net30 for vendor purchases, and that Finance generally avoids card charges for enterprise contracts.
- Contract routing: should we expect a redline from your legal team or will Procurement accept our standard SOW + MSA?
- Marketplace preference: are you open to transacting through AWS Marketplace (saves procurement paperwork) or do you need a direct Redwood contract?

2) Commercial path options (to align packaging with your purchasing rules):
- Hosted (on-demand): lowest friction for pilot; pay-as-you-go, can start on card or invoiced with PO. Good if you need quick time-to-value.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended if you expect sustained throughput and want predictable unit economics. Typically by monthly/annual commit with invoice+PO.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated data or on-prem compliance — longer procurement + security review, usually enterprise term.

3) Pricing/commit considerations:
- Pilot recommendation: start hosted on on-demand credits for 4–6 weeks to validate quality/latency. If usage stabilizes, convert to a small committed Dedicated pool (3–6 mo commit) to lower unit costs.
- We can provide a 90‑day credit program or initial discounted commit to help bridge pilot procurement timelines.

4) Action items I propose:
- Sofia: confirm preferred procurement route (PO vs card vs marketplace) and whether Legal will need to send redlines.
- James: share procurement contact and billing info if PO path.
- Redwood (Avery/Dylan/Me): we'll attach a short pricing matrix and procurement checklist and schedule a follow-up with procurement/legal if helpful.

Attaching a draft pricing matrix + procurement checklist for your review. Happy to jump on a quick call with Procurement next week to speed this along.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0174
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps (procurement & commercial path)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers from Procurement / Finance perspective: 

- Payment method: Procurement prefers PO + Net30 for vendors. Card is only for small one-off purchases under $5k.
- Marketplace: We like AWS Marketplace for simplified invoicing, but Legal still requires a vendor master & insurance docs. If Redwood can offer AWS Marketplace procurement, that would remove some internal approvals.
- Contract: Legal will likely want to review and redline an MSA (standard process). We can route redlines back to you — upload preferred contract to DocuSign or share via email.

I'll introduce our Procurement lead (copied in) if needed — James handles vendor setup and billing. We can target a PO for the pilot if we have an agreed price and SOW.

Next steps for us:
- James: can you share vendor setup form and billing address?
- Marissa: if you can provide a 30-day pilot pricing for hosted (on-demand) and a committed 6-month dedicated estimate, that will help Finance sign-off.

Appreciate it —
Sofia

Sofia Martinez
Director, Procurement | Acme Retail
sofia.martinez@acmeretail.com
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps (procurement & commercial path)

Hi Sofia / team —

Quick technical/commercial note to help sizing the Dedicated vs Hosted estimates: 
- For the pilot use-case (catalog summarization + search reranking), estimated steady-state token throughput is ~10M tokens/day if the pilot scales across 3 markets.
- Hosted (on-demand) estimate: we can provide a per-token run-rate for the pilot (see attached matrix) — this is straightforward to invoice via PO. Latency targets met with hosted for pilot volumes.
- Dedicated: a small 4-GPU Dedicated pool (A100 equiv) with modest commit reduces per-token cost by ~35% vs on-demand; commits are typically monthly or annual, billed via invoice/PO.
- Private: if you need VPC/private, procurement lead time is longer and we'll need your security questionnaire answers; usually results in an enterprise contract and onboarding fee.

If Procurement needs an official quote document, Marissa and I can prepare a PO-ready quote with line-item pricing and billing terms (Net30) tomorrow.

- Avery Johnson
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Sofia and Avery. Proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Redwood to send a PO-ready quote (hosted 30-day pilot pricing + optional 6-month small Dedicated commit) and a short SOW by EOD tomorrow.
2) Sofia to confirm vendor setup fields and preferred billing address so we can populate the quote.
3) If Acme prefers AWS Marketplace, we can include marketplace pricing and a note on the vendor setup benefits. Marketplace will speed procurement but requires vendor master/insurance.
4) Schedule a 30-minute procurement handoff next week (Marissa + Avery + James + your Procurement lead) to finalize PO details and contract routing.

If that looks good, I'll send the quote and SOW and attach the procurement checklist for James to start vendor setup.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.
